goal: The dash node is laid out with the real parts, proved in cardboard in the car, and its carrier panels are cut, deburred and painted.
where: bench, then the driver footwell and under the dash for the mock-up
tools:
Cardboard, marker, craft knife, tape
Steel rule and square
Drill and bits, step bit
Jigsaw or hacksaw, files, deburring tool
Centre punch
Phone camera
before:
E12 - the car starts and charges on the new backbone
C2 - the panel stock (P090) and paint (P093) are bought
C1's measurements in hand: the M-1 dash envelope and the wideband gauge's hiding place
The interior is still out (S1), so the footwell and dash rail are open
Master disconnect open while you reach around the temporary distribution post: the 2 AWG feed is live there (E10, E4)
know:
The dash node is everything that hangs off the PMU in one place: the PMU-24, the always-hot busbar, the ground bus, fuse blocks A and B, the inline fuse holders, nine relay sockets, the wake strip, a perfboard and the wideband gauge [work E13]
Nine relay sockets at the node, not seven: K1 K2 K3 K4 K11 K12 K13 and the two seat relays K14 K15 added by D-469 [relays K14, K15]
Sixteen receptacles sit at the dash post: L1-P DTP04-4P, L1-S1 DT04-12P, L1-S2 DT04-12P, L2-P DTP04-4P, L2-M DT04-8P, L2-S DT04-6P, L3-P DTP04-2P, L3-M DT04-2P, L3-S1 DT04-12P, L3-S2 DT04-12P, L3-S3 DT04-8P, L4-P DTP04-4P, L4-M DT04-12P, L4-S DT04-8P, L4-S2 DT04-8P, L2-R DT04-4P [housings]
Leave panel room beside L1-S1 / L1-S2 for four more DT04-12P receptacles for the engine swap - five if engine block 02.16 was answered (a) [work E13, engine D-443]
Water runs down from the cowl seam and the windscreen corners: every wire enters the PMU and the node from below or with a drip loop, nothing mounts in the lowest 50 mm of the footwell, and the PMU 39-way faces down or sideways, never up [rules water-ingress]
What CK04 found (where the water goes with the dash out) moves a bracket now for free [checks CK04]
The PMU stands on three M6 x 12 mm stand-offs for airflow [parts P060]
The busbar is the Blue Sea 2300, 10-gang 150 A with cover: one always-hot bar and one ground bus, both covered [parts P007]
The DCU tail must reach the centre stack: the node has to sit close enough along RT11, which is measured at M-2 [routes RT11, housings DP-DCU-B]
Receptacle clips: 1027-003-1200 fits the 2, 4, 6 and 12-way and every DTP; the 8-way receptacles take the 8-way clip - four of them are at the post (L2-M, L3-S3, L4-S, L4-S2), D1 and D2 are at the sill; both use an 11 mm hole - confirm on the clip in hand [parts P030, P162]
Nothing here is measured by anyone but you: the cardboard in the car is the proof, not the drawing [R11]
done_when: Every part has a place on painted panels that passed the cardboard mock-up in the car: the PMU lever swings its full arc, there is 60 mm clear behind every receptacle, both fuse blocks can be reached, and nothing sits in the lowest 50 mm.
if_not: If it does not all fit inside the M-1 space, do not thin the clearances: split it across more panels or move a panel, mock it again, and raise a note in the app with a photo. If RT11 is long for the DCU tail, raise a note before cutting metal.
record: Tick the row. Add a note with the photos of the cardboard mock-up in the car and the finished panels.

Torque wrench 1/4 in drive, 2-20 N·m (P046)
Wire strippers and flush cutters (P043)
Label printer with the node labels from E6 (P041)
Paint pen (P082)
before:
E13 - the panels are cut and painted
E6 - the node labels are printed
Nothing is connected to the car: this is bench work
know:
The PMU stands on three M6 stand-offs [work E14, parts P060]
Five 40 A-class MAXI holders (P189): F30 feeds block A, F31 feeds K11 terminal 30, F32 sits at K11 terminal 87 and feeds block B - 40 A fuses (P190); F35 and F36 feed the seat relays K14 / K15 - 25 A fuses (P191) [fuses F30, F31, F32, F35, F36, D-467, D-469]
The fuse sits at the bar so the only wire protected by the Class-T alone is a short stub: each busbar-fed inline holder (F12, F22, F23) has its 14 AWG lead cut to about 50 mm, never more than 180 mm [node_conductors N75, N87]
Block A is on the busbar: position 1 F2, 2 F3, 3 F19, 4 F13 (no fuse). Block B is behind K11: position 1 F1, 2 F5 (no fuse) [fuses]
The 8-position strip is full: seven wake inputs and the common rail [parts P068]
Labels come from the label columns: K1 POPUP-L · K2 POPUP-R · K3 HATCH-REL · K4 FUEL-REL · K11 HEAD-UNIT · K12 WASHER · K13 FUEL-PUMP · K14 SEAT-D · K15 SEAT-P [relays]

record: Tick the row.

goal: The wake strip carries its seven diodes and bleed resistor, the two wake sense stages are built on the perfboard to the wake_stages table, the two bias resistors are fitted, and the bench check CK12 is read.
where: bench
tools:
Soldering iron and solder (P044)
Flush cutters, needle-nose pliers (P043)
Multimeter: ohms, diode test, DC volts (P045)
Heat gun (P042)
A 12 V bench supply or the battery through a fused lead for CK12
before:
E14 - the strip and perfboard are mounted
A10 - the stage values are in the record (they are: the wake_stages table)
Eye protection while soldering and clipping leads
know:
The PMU wakes when pin 7 (+12V SW) goes high. Seven sources are OR-ed onto it through one diode each, so no source can feed another [pins 7]
Strip inputs: 1 ACC (L3-S1 12) · 2 RUN (L3-S2 1) · 3 door stage · 4 horn / hazard / wink stage · 5 O22 keep-alive (pin 8) · 6 brake plunger (L3-S1 7) · 7 DCU wake request (DP-DCU 6) [node_conductors N33-N37, N63, N76]
Seven 1N5819, band (cathode) toward the common rail; the rail goes to pin 7; 10 kΩ from the rail to the GND bus [node_conductors N38, work E15]
The two sense stages are a comparator design now: one LM2903 DIP-8 serves both, U1A the door line (A6, pin 18), U1B the horn / hazard / wink line (A8, pin 19). The work row still says NPN sense stages: the table is newer and wins [wake_stages WS15, WS25]
Both stages are fed from F23, 3 A, constant from the busbar [fuses F23, node_conductors N87]
The base clamps are 1N4148, never a Schottky: a 1N5819 leaks hot and loses the pulse at 85 °C [wake_stages WS19]
The edge capacitors are 2.2 µF film (P158); the value is still to be confirmed against the PMU boot time CK12 reads [wake_stages WS17]
The threshold divider resistors WS14 / WS24 are 1 % parts [wake_stages WS14]
Bias: 100 kΩ from pin 15 (+5 V) to pin 35 (A15) and 100 kΩ from pin 15 to pin 22 (A16), so a broken wire reads 0, not OFF [node_conductors N39]
At rest the door and A8 lines sit at 0.166 x the F23 voltage (about 1.99 V at 12.0 V); the comparator threshold is 0.115 x [wake_stages WS12, WS13]
The pin-out of the LM2903 and the 2N3904 is not in the record: read each off its datasheet before soldering [gap]
done_when: Seven diodes read forward toward the rail and blocked the other way; every resistor measured before fitting; CK12 read on the bench: at rest no wake, any door or A8 switch wakes, the three unknowns (i)-(iii) written down.
if_not: A stage that does not wake: check the comparator supply (F23) and the divider node (0.115 x F23), then the 2.2 µF and the follower. If the unpowered PMU pin reads under 200 kΩ to ground at CK12 (i), stop: WS12 may have to drop - raise a note with the reading. Do not put the node in the car on a failing CK12.
record: Tick the row. Enter the CK12 readings as a note: (i) ohms pin 18 and pin 19 to ground with the PMU unpowered, (ii) the lowest pin 7 voltage that switches the PMU on and its current at 12 V, (iii) seconds from pin 7 high to O22 on.

goal: All 39 cavities of the PMU connector are terminated, locked and pull-tested, each on 18 in of labelled wire.
where: bench
tools:
Open-barrel ratchet crimper, 1.5 mm and 2.8 mm dies (P039)
Wire strippers and flush cutters (P043)
Paint pen (P082)
Label printer (P041)
Heat gun for the label shrink (P042)
Good light and a magnifier
before:
E15 - the wake parts are built
CK24 read at M-1: the terminal part numbers on the spare PMU housings (1.5 mm and 2.8 mm) and which terminal pin 15 takes
Practice crimps pulled on scrap with this crimper and these terminals
The connector is off the PMU and nothing is powered
Eye protection
know:
The PMU-24 has one 39-way connector plus the +12 V stud. Every one of the 39 positions is used [rules spare-capacity]
Three cavity sizes: 11 large (pins 1, 2, 12, 13, 14, 25, 26, 27, 28, 38, 39 - the 2.8 mm die), 27 small (the 1.5 mm die) and one medium, pin 15, whose terminal and die the record does not name - confirm from CK24 [parts P039, checks CK24]
Cavity numbers are the numbers moulded into the connector itself: read them off the part, never mirror a drawing [rules cavity-numbers]
Colours by family: RED power outputs, ORN the 15 A outputs on 14 AWG, GRY analog inputs, BLU wake, PNK the +5 V reference, YEL / GRN CAN high / low, BLK ground [colours]
Large pins carry up to 25 A, the 14 AWG ORN pins 15 A, the 16 AWG RED output pins 7 A [pins hw_max_a]
The +12 V stud is not in this connector: it takes the 2 AWG from the busbar at E17 / E24 [pins STUD]
Pin 25, the ground, lands on the GND bus within 6 in: it is the one wire that will be cut shorter than 18 in when it lands [pins 25]
The two CAN pairs are hand-twisted: 23 with 36 (CAN1), 24 with 37 (CAN2) [colours, pins 23, 24]
It is terminated once and never reopened [work E16]
The SICMA terminals have no parts row and no strip length in the record: use the terminals that came with the PMU connector and the strip length your practice crimps proved [gap]
done_when: 39 wires, each labelled, each clicked in and pulled; the secondary lock is on; no wire moves under a firm pull; the lever latched once fully on the PMU with a clear arc.
if_not: A terminal that does not click or pulls out: do not force it and do not re-use it - cut it off, crimp a new one. A wire in the wrong cavity: stop, do not pick at it with a pin - raise a note; the record names no removal tool for this connector.
record: Tick the row.

goal: Every node conductor is run, spliced and landed, every receptacle at the post is pinned, plugged and wedge-locked, and the ICU and DCU tails are made.
where: bench
tools:
Deutsch solid-contact 4-indent crimper, sizes 12 / 16 (P038)
Ratchet crimper for heat-shrink terminals and butt splices (P171)
Open-barrel crimper for the relay socket terminals (P039)
Wire strippers, flush cutters (P043)
Heat gun (P042)
Soldering iron (P044)
Contact removal tools, size 16 (P031, P032)
Label printer (P041)
Multimeter on continuity (P045)
Torque wrench (P046)
before:
E16 - the 39-way is terminated
E15 - the wake strip and stages are built
CK08 (M-3, the pop-up motors) is read before the pop-up conductors N08-N15 and N105 are landed
Nothing is powered; the 39-way is off the PMU
Eye protection for crimping
know:
A receptacle is the box-side half (DT04 / DTP04, pin contacts); the leg plugs (DT06, socket contacts) are made at E20-E23 [housings]
Every splice at the node is a sealed crimp butt splice with adhesive heat-shrink [work E17, parts P078]
An unfused tap off an output is 14 AWG up to its fuse (the holder's own lead), 16 AWG after it [node_conductors N19, N85]
CAN2 never leaves the dash: one twisted pair from pins 24 / 37 to a splice, pairs on to DP-ICU-A 4 / 5, DP-DCU 4 / 5 and the wideband gauge, and a 120 Ω resistor at the end of the run [node_conductors N55, N74, D-346]
The A4 and A5 inputs carry the inhibitor switch alone since D-487: pin 17 goes to L1-S1 11 only and pin 31 to L1-S2 7 only. Rows N40 / N41 still name L2-S 1 / 2, which are the pop-up up commands now [cavities L2-S 1, L2-S 2, pins 17, 31]
The DCU plugs in later (E26): its two tails end in DT06 plugs at the centre stack and are dust-capped until then [housings DP-DCU, DP-DCU-B, D-472]
The ICU tails are 150 mm from the post [housings DP-ICU-A, D-270]
The DCU tail length is the post to centre-stack run RT11 and the DP-DIAG tail is the run to the glovebox RT12: neither is measured - confirm [routes RT11, RT12]
DT size-16 contacts seal on 14-20 AWG and carry 13 A; DTP size-12 contacts seal on 10-14 AWG and carry 25 A [series DT, DTP]
The seat-feed tails (N108, N109, N112) and the comfort grounds (N102) are routed at E38: at this row their relays are wired and the tails left labelled [work E38]
The load-dump TVS (P136) goes across the PMU main feed at the module; no row says which way round or on which studs - read its datasheet [parts P136, gap]
done_when: Every row of node_conductors is in place and labelled at both ends, every receptacle cavity holds a pin or a sealing plug, every wedgelock is in, the two ICU tails and the two DCU tails end in plugs.
if_not: A contact in the wrong cavity: release it with the removal tool (P031 / P032), never pull the wire. A conductor with no home in the lists: stop and raise a note - do not improvise a splice.
record: Tick the row.

goal: The finished node is proved: every PMU cavity reaches what the tables say and nothing else, nothing leaks to ground, the relays and fuses are fitted, every wire is labelled and the panels are photographed.
where: bench
tools:
Multimeter with a continuity beeper and a megohm range (P045)
Two sharp probe leads and a back-probe pin that fits a DT pin without spreading a socket
The pin list on the laptop or phone
Phone camera
before:
E17 - every conductor is landed
The 39-way is off the PMU; no leg, relay or fuse is fitted; the node is not powered
know:
Continuity is taken with the meter on its beeper [work E18]
Isolation means open: more than 1 MΩ. Any lower reading is a stray strand [work E18]
Nine relays at the node, all the same part (P003): K1 K2 K3 K4 K11 K12 K13 K14 K15. The work row lists five and calls K3 / K4 the luxury package's; the relays table has all nine fitted this build [relays, parts P003, D-451, D-469]
Blade fuses come from the drawer, one of every rating in the fuses table [parts P141]
Two blade positions stay empty and keep their labels: F13 (block A position 4) and F5 (block B position 2) [fuses F13, F5]
Through a diode the beeper is one-way: the wake strip inputs and the O2 / O3 pop-up coil taps read as a diode, not as a short [node_conductors N09, N38]
Pin 15 reaches pins 35 and 22 through 100 kΩ each and the oil node through 100 Ω: that is correct, not a fault [node_conductors N39]
The CAN2 pair should read about 120 Ω with nothing plugged in: the one resistor at the node [node_conductors N74]
done_when: All 39 cavities pass continuity and the three must-not-reach touches each; every power cavity reads open to its neighbours and to the ground bus; nine relays and every LIVE fuse are in; photos taken.
if_not: A missing continuity: find it now - a contact not seated or a splice not crimped. Any isolation reading under 1 MΩ: stop and find the strand before any power is applied. Do not go on to E19 with an open item.
record: Tick the row. Add the photos as a note.

goal: The sleeping current of the finished dash node is measured and is 50 mA or less.
where: bench
tools:
Multimeter with a fused 10 A range and a mA range (P045)
A 12 V supply for the node through a fused lead
before:
E18 - the node passed continuity and isolation, relays and fuses fitted
CK12 read (E15)
No leg plugged in; the DCU tails capped
know:
Target 30 mA or less; accept 50 mA or less [work E19, loads LD17, D-280]
What should be drawing: the PMU asleep (no manual figure; a bench report says under 20 mA) and the wake stages (under 0.2 mA). K11 is open when asleep. The DCU is not plugged in yet [loads LD17]
The PMU sleeps when nothing on the wake strip is high; with no key, door or A8 input the keep-alive drops 30 s after the last change [rules sleep]
On a 40 Ah pack 150 mA is about 11 days and 20 mA about 80 days [checks CK02]
This is the PMU's share; the whole-car figure is read later at E29 [checks CK02]
It cannot be re-taken once the dash is closed without undoing the install [work E19]
The record does not name the bench supply for this test, nor what configuration the PMU carries before E25: with pin 7 low it should be asleep - confirm [gap]
done_when: A steady reading of 50 mA or less with the PMU asleep, entered in the app.
if_not: Above 50 mA: lift the wake-strip branches one at a time (inputs 1 to 7, then F23, F22, F12) and watch the reading to find the branch. Do not close the dash on a failing number: raise a note with the readings.
record: Enter the reading in mA (this row takes a value).

goal: Harness leg L3, the dash leg, is cut, labelled, pinned into its five plugs, ended at its switches and branch receptacles, and tested end to end.
where: bench - a board or floor long enough for the full-scale layout
tools:
Deutsch solid-contact 4-indent crimper, sizes 12 / 16 (P038)
Wire strippers 10-22 AWG, flush cutters (P043)
Ratchet crimper for heat-shrink butt splices, rings and spades (P171)
Heat gun (P042)
Soldering iron and solder (P044)
Multimeter: continuity beeper, ohms (P045)
Label printer with flexible-ID tape (P041)
Contact removal tools, size 16 (P031, P032) and size 12 (P033)
Tape measure, and a board or floor long enough to lay the leg full-scale
Paint pen (P082)
before:
E19 - the dash node passed its sleeping-current test
G13 - the cut lengths are derived from the measured routes (C1, M-2)
E7 - the ladder resistor sub-assemblies are built and bagged
CK10 read: the ignition switch IG contact holds through START - take it before this leg is crimped
CK17 and CK18 read: the light switch and stalk contact tables - the ladders are built to what they found
E5 - Deutsch practice done
Eye protection for crimping and clipping
know:
Cut length is 1.5 x the measured route; the margin is that factor, no extra loop is added [rules cut-list, D-202]
Every wire is labelled at both ends the moment it is cut, printed tape, the same pair read in opposite order: O8 / L2-M-1 at one end, L2-M-1 / O8 at the other; a capped far end reads <cavity> / CAPPED [rules label-format]
The leg side is the PLUG (DT06 / DTP06) and takes SOCKET contacts; a branch-end receptacle (DT04 / DTP04) takes PIN contacts [housings, work E20]
A CAPPED wire is cut, labelled and terminated exactly like a LIVE one [work E20]
Cavity numbers are the ones moulded into the housing: read them off the part [rules cavity-numbers]
DT size-16 contacts take 14-20 AWG and carry 13 A; DTP size-12 contacts take 10-14 AWG and carry 25 A [series DT, DTP]
Where a device keeps its factory plug, the plug is cut from the old harness with 150 mm of factory lead and each lead is joined to its new wire with a sealed butt splice; a stud or blade gets a heat-shrink ring or spade [rules device-end]
The factory plugs stay on the old harness until their circuit migrates (E27 / E28): the record does not say at which row each factory-lead splice is made, so at the bench those ends are left cut to length, labelled and insulated [work E27, E28, gap]
L3 has five plugs at the post - L3-P, L3-M, L3-S1, L3-S2, L3-S3 - and four branch-end receptacles: L3-BLW at the HVAC case, L3-CMF behind the centre stack, L3-MOD and L3-RDR behind the dash [housings]
L3-S2 3-6 and L3-S3 5-8 are sealing plugs: the window commands and mirror lines run in the DCU tail from the node, not in this leg [cavities L3-S2 3, L3-S3 5, D-472]
The seat receptacles and comfort-return harness (L3-SD, L3-SP, L3-SDM, L3-SPM) are E38 and the speaker runs are E41: not this row [work E38, E41]
F24, 3 A sealed inline, sits in the leg behind the lower dash where the light-switch and brake-wake branch leaves the L3-S2 2 wire [fuses F24, D-412]
The ignition switch is a new electrical portion (1981-83 type, P086); the light switch, both stalks and the horn pad are the car's own, kept [devices DV18, DV19, DV20, DV22, DV23]
The wiper stalk WASH contact carries two wires: the ladder leg to L3-S1 4 and a plain wire to L3-S2 9, the washer relay coil return [devices DV22, work E20]
WASH leg value: the ladders table says 470 Ω + 1N4148; the cavity and device rows still say 1.8 kΩ + 1N5819. Build to the E7 sub-assembly made from the ladders table - confirm before soldering [ladders A2 WASH, cavities L3-S1 4]
Horn 8.2 kΩ and the two wink resistors (18 kΩ left, 33 kΩ right) all join onto the L3-S1 11 wire; the wink resistors are on the plate board, and the plate's 4-way header J2 gives pin 1 → L3-S1 9, pin 2 → L3-S1 10, pin 3 → L3-S1 11, pin 4 → dash ground [devices DV24, D-504]
The hazard switch gets a 47 kΩ baseline to column ground at the switch, beside its 4.7 kΩ [cavities L3-S1 6, D-368]
The brake wake is a spare adjustable plunger switch (P084) on the pedal, fed through F24, not the brake lamp switch [cavities L3-S1 7, D-278]
Ladder check: each state within 2 % of its table value at the leg-side cavity [work E20]
Column and pedal fasteners, clip counts and the factory wire colours at the kept switches are not in this row's tables: the device rows give the terminal by function only [gap]
done_when: Every L3 cavity is continuous to its own far end and to nothing else, isolation is open, each ladder state fitted so far reads within 2 % of its value, every end is labelled, branch receptacles are dust-capped, and the leg is bundled every 150 mm but not wrapped.
if_not: A contact in the wrong cavity: release it with the removal tool, never pull the wire. A ladder state off by more than 2 %: measure the resistor alone, then the joint. A length that comes up short on the layout: stop, re-measure the route, raise a note.
record: Tick the row.

The main feed is C03: 2 AWG red from the Class-T through the tunnel, about 16 ft - confirm. Its lug lands on the always-hot busbar stud. Busbar to the PMU stud is C10, 2 AWG, about 0.7 ft - confirm [cables C03, C10; node_conductors N01]
Ground: PMU pin 25 to the ground bus on 10 AWG black, 6 in or less; the ground bus to the dash chassis star on 10 AWG black, about 2 ft - confirm; bare metal, star washer, cavity wax [node_conductors N57, N58; grounds G14]
The Class-T fuse is 150 A, in its block in the cargo bin beside the master disconnect [fuses Class-T]
First power goes through a 5 A fuse bridged across the Class-T block's two terminals, so a short at the node melts a 5 A fuse and not 2 AWG cable [work E24]
DP-DIAG is the laptop port, a 4-way Deutsch DT in the glovebox: 1 CAN1 high (yellow), 2 CAN1 low (green), 3 +12 V constant through F2 (2 A), 4 ground. 120 ohm sits across 1 and 2 inside the plug and 120 ohm across PMU pins 23 and 36 [cavities DP-DIAG 1-4; fuses F2; node_conductors N56]
CAN1 is the laptop bus, fixed at 1 Mbps [recovery RC03]
The PMU switches on when pin 7 (+12V SW, the wake strip's common rail) is high. With no leg plugged in the record names nothing that lifts pin 7 - confirm what wakes it [pins 7]
P136 is the load-dump TVS, a surge clamp from the busbar to the dash star. The part is not chosen yet: 18-20 V standoff, 5 kW or more, bolt-down - confirm [parts P136]
DP-DCU cavity 1 is live as soon as the busbar is (F22, 3 A, constant). Its plug stays dust-capped until E26 [housings DP-DCU; fuses F22]
Torque for every heavy stud is the maker's figure read at D1. No figure is in the record yet - confirm [rules torque]
The factory harness's main feed keeps its factory fusible links in series: the 1.25 sq main link and the brown 0.3 sq links [work E11; 00-CAR PT316, PT317]
done_when: The node does not move when pushed; with the 150 A Class-T fuse back in and the disconnect closed, the client shows the PMU-24 over DP-DIAG with every output disabled; nothing is warm, nothing smells; the factory circuits work from the busbar as they did at E12.
if_not: The 5 A fuse blows: open the disconnect and find the short at the node with E18's isolation test before another fuse goes in. Never fit the Class-T fuse to find out. The client does not see the PMU: measure 12 V at the PMU stud and at pin 7 (recovery RC06); check 120 ohm at both ends of CAN1 and F2. Anything else: raise it in the app as a note.
record: Tick E24 in the app. No value. Add a note saying what lifted pin 7 for the first power-up and which TVS part was fitted.

goal: The whole PMU configuration from the record is entered in the client and saved as RevA-01, with every output still disabled and no current limit set.
where: in the car: laptop on the passenger side, plugged into DP-DIAG in the glovebox
tools:
Camden's Windows laptop with ECUMaster's PMU client (D-376)
USB-to-CAN interface cable (P138)
a charger on the battery or an eye on its voltage: the node is live for hours with the engine off
before:
E24 done: the PMU answers over DP-DIAG
No harness leg plugged in
Every output disabled, and it stays that way through this whole row
The bench session's three answers in hand: CK06 (the Delayed turn off range), CK13 (timeouts in fractions of a second) and CK15 (whether a function can divide)
know:
The configuration is the record itself: names and channels from pins, states from inputs and ladders, expressions from logic, retry behaviour from rules, the bus from can_messages [work E25]
22 outputs. O1-O5 and O12-O16 are the 25 A pins. O6-O11 are the 15 A pins. O17-O22 are the 7 A pins: they are the analog pins A9-A14 set up as outputs [pins; inputs A9-A14]
Ten inputs. A1-A8 are the 0-5 V ladder inputs, read as 0-1023 counts. A15 and A16 are the two ladders fed from battery voltage, each with a 100 kOhm bias from pin 15 (+5 V) [rules ladder-decode; node_conductors N39]
No decode window is typed today. Windows are read live in the car at E26 and E27 and entered then [D-142]
No current limit today. The enable-at limits go in at E26 [work E25]
CAN1 is the laptop bus at 1 Mbps. CAN2 is the car's bus at 500 kbps, 11-bit ids, with the PMU's software termination ON [pins 23, 24; params can_bitrate]
The PMU's four frames 0x100, 0x110, 0x120 and 0x130 are a CANbus Export we define, byte by byte [D-378; can_fields]
Wire is control and CAN is telemetry: the only bus values the PMU acts on are the panel keys in frame 0x400 - rear defog, hatch, fuel door and the window keys [D-251; can_messages 0x400]
OIL_MIN, the oil-pressure count the fuel-pump gate compares against, is not entered today. It is read in the car at the first idle [logic FUEL_PUMP]
The pop-up cycle's idle-current threshold is not typed today either. It comes from CK08's powered readings and is entered when the pop-ups move, MG15 [rules pop-up-cycle]
The PMU has a built-in inertia switch that drops every output above a set acceleration, 6 G by default [work G3]
Saved files come back to the project by hand if they are to be kept [D-376]
done_when: RevA-01 is saved in the PMU and on the laptop; every output is named, has its expression and retry setting, and is disabled; no Max Current limit is entered; the client reports no error on any function.
if_not: The client refuses a function as written: use the fallback its check names - CK15 for the division, CK13 for timeouts, CK06 for the keep-alive timer - and say which in a note. An expression the record does not settle: do not improvise it; leave that output without logic, disabled, and raise it in the app as a note.
record: Tick E25 in the app. No value. A note for every place the client forced a different form than the record's expression.

goal: The dash leg L3, the instrument unit (ICU) and the climate unit (DCU) are plugged in, every column-switch position lands in its own decode window, the enable-at limits are entered, and still no output is enabled.
where: dash post, steering column, binnacle (the instrument opening) and the centre-stack opening
tools:
Camden's Windows laptop with ECUMaster's PMU client (D-376)
USB-to-CAN interface cable (P138)
multimeter: DC volts, ohms, continuity beeper (P045)
fuse puller, for F3 and F24
a helper is useful: one works the switches, one reads the screen
before:
E25 done: RevA-01 saved
F6 done: the climate unit commissioned on the bench
F3 done: the display chain proven on the bench
Master disconnect OPEN while the plugs go in
Every output disabled, and it stays so through this row
From this row the key and the column switches feed the PMU. The car does not start again until the last circuit has moved at the end of E28, and it is not driven until E35
know:
L3 has five plugs at the dash post: L3-P (DTP 2-way), L3-M (DT 2-way), L3-S1 (DT 12-way), L3-S2 (DT 12-way) and L3-S3 (DT 8-way). Every housing carries its code on both halves [housings L3-P, L3-M, L3-S1, L3-S2, L3-S3; rules label-format]
The instrument unit sits in the binnacle with the display on its face. Two tails from the dash post plug into its rear wall: DP-ICU-A, a 6-way, and DP-ICU-B, a 12-way [housings DP-ICU-A, DP-ICU-B; D-491]
The climate unit is one box in the centre-stack opening with the control panel on its face and the DCU inside. Two tails plug into its rear wall now: DP-DCU, a 6-way, and DP-DCU-B, a 12-way [housings DP-DCU, DP-DCU-B; D-479]
DP-DCU cavity 1 is constant 12 V through F22 (3 A): the climate unit is alive the moment it is plugged in. The instrument unit's logic is on O10 and stays dark until that output is enabled [cavities DP-DCU 1, DP-ICU-A 1]
The climate unit's loads are not in the car yet, so its outputs drive capped lines [work E26]
Window half-widths, in counts: A1 55 - A2 45 - A3 30 - A4 20 - A5 20 - A6 20 - A8 35 - A15 75 - A16 200 [inputs]
A state's window is its live reading plus and minus the half-width. A reading that falls between windows is a wiring fault to fix now [work E26; rules ladder-decode]
A15 and A16 decode on conductance: read OFF first and refit k2 = k1 x the OFF reading, so OFF gives g = 0 [rules ladder-decode]
A dead switch feed must read as a FAULT, not as OFF: proven by pulling F3 at ACC and F24 at PARK [rules ladder-decode; D-412]
F3 is 5 A in block A position 2 at the dash node. F24 is 3 A, a sealed inline holder behind the lower dash panel where the light-switch branch leaves the leg [fuses F3, F24]
The wiper stalk's WASH leg: the ladders table has 470 ohm plus a 1N4148 diode; the cavity row still says 1.8 kOhm plus a 1N5819. What E20 built is what is there: read it, do not assume [ladders A2 WASH; cavities L3-S1 4]
A3 to A7 (brake and park, the gear lever, the doors, oil pressure) are not read today: they need L2, L4 and L1, at E27 [work E26]
done_when: Every position of the key, light switch, dimmer, pass, turn stalk, hazard, wiper stalk, wash, horn pad and both wink buttons shows its own named state in the client with no overlap and no FAULT; pulling F3 and F24 each gives a FAULT; the enable-at limits are entered; a new revision is saved; no output is enabled.
if_not: A reading between two windows, or two positions reading the same: it is a wiring fault at that switch - a resistor on the wrong contact or a missing ground. Unplug L3-S1, measure ohms from the leg-side cavity to ground in each position and compare with the ladder's resistor. A reading of 0 or over 990: an open or short on that wire. The climate unit silent on the bus: check F22 and the two CAN2 cavities. Do not widen a window to make a bad reading fit.
record: Tick E26 in the app. No value. The readings live in the configuration; save it as a new revision and note the revision name.

goal: The front leg L2, the rear leg L4 with the sill node, and the engine leg L1 are routed, clipped, grommeted and plugged into the dash post, F17 is fitted and the start relay K9 wired, and the brake, gear-lever and door inputs are read into their windows - with every load still on the factory harness.
where: engine bay, nose, cowl, tunnel, driver sill, cargo area, and the dash post
tools:
P-clips, grommets, split loom and pull string (P081)
cloth harness tape (P080) - a turn every 150 mm, no final wrap
drill and bits for P-clip fixings - sizes are not in the record
ratchet crimper for heat-shrink ring terminals (P171), for K9's 10 AWG rings
heat gun (P042)
torque wrench 1/4 in drive, 2-20 N-m (P046)
multimeter: DC volts, ohms, continuity beeper (P045)
Camden's Windows laptop with ECUMaster's PMU client (D-376)
USB-to-CAN interface cable (P138)
jack and jack stands, wheel chocks - for the run under the floor to the tank
before:
E26 done: L3, the instrument unit and the climate unit are in and their inputs read
Master disconnect OPEN for all routing and for anything at the starter stud
Jack stands under the car and wheels chocked before going underneath. Park is not a parking brake
No sparks near the tank; extinguisher within reach
The car does not start during this row (D-414)
know:
L2 leaves the dash post through the cowl grommet and runs along the inner wing to a splice point at the nose. The 3D model estimates 11.4 ft; the leg was cut from the length measured at M-2 [routes RT06]
From the nose: across the radiator support to each headlight bucket and pop-up motor; to the front combo lamps, side markers and horns; and back along the cowl to the wiper motor and washer pump, which sit at the cowl [routes RT07, RT08, RT09]
L4 runs through the tunnel to the rear node in the cargo bin, beside the three heavy cables. A branch in the tunnel goes to the transmission for the road-speed sensor and the kick-down solenoid [routes RT15, RT21]
From the rear node: along both quarters to the tail, licence and marker lamps; under the floor to the fuel pump and tank sender; through the hatch hinge loop to the hatch release, luggage lamp and defog grid; up the C-pillar to the interior lamp; behind the driver-side quarter trim to the fuel-door solenoid [routes RT16, RT17, RT18, RT23, RT24, RT25]
The sill run goes from the dash post along the driver sill to the sill node, a small panel behind the driver kick panel [routes RT19; devices DV43]
L1 leaves through the firewall grommet on the passenger side to a junction in the engine bay, then branches: coils and igniters along the upper rear housing, alternator down the front of the block, the two senders at the rear housing, starter and inhibitor switch under the intake, brake-fluid switch along the firewall [routes RT01, RT02, RT03, RT04, RT05, RT26]
The shielded tach wire crosses ignition leads at 90 degrees and never runs beside one within 50 mm. Signal bundles L2-S and L4-S run apart from the power bundles L2-P and L4-P [rules emc-routing; housings L2-S; cavities L4-S 1]
Every bundle enters a node from below or with a drip loop [rules water-ingress]
The fuel pump's ground is its own 12 AWG wire to the rear star stud, never shared [grounds G26]
K9, the start relay, is a sealed relay in a weatherproof socket on the inner fender. 86 from L1-S1 1; 85 to block ground, 16 AWG black; 30 from F17 on 10 AWG red, about 4 ft - confirm; 87 to the starter's small S terminal on 10 AWG red, about 3 ft - confirm [relays K9; cables C08, C09; grounds G02]
F17 is a 30 A MIDI fuse in a bolt-down holder beside the starter's main stud. The holder went in at E10 and was left unwired [fuses F17; work E10]
A3 decodes upward, half-width 30: IDLE 47 kOhm, PARKED 12 kOhm beside it, BRAKE 4.7 kOhm beside it, BRAKE+PARKED both [ladders A3; inputs A3]
A4 and A5 decode upward, half-width 20: IDLE 47 kOhm; CRANK_OK and REVERSE add 8.2 kOhm beside it. A6, half-width 20: CLOSED 47 kOhm, DRV adds 24 kOhm and a diode, PASS adds 8.2 kOhm and a diode, BOTH adds both [ladders A4, A5, A6; inputs A4, A5, A6]
Looms are not final-wrapped today: the cabin's at E35, the engine bay's at E33 after the first heat cycles [work E35, E33]
done_when: All ten leg plugs are latched at the dash post; every run is clipped, grommeted at each pass-through and clear of heat and moving parts; F17 is in and K9 is wired; A3, A4, A5 and A6 each show the right named state for every position that is connected; a new revision is saved; nothing is enabled.
if_not: A leg that will not reach: do not stretch or re-splice it - note the shortfall in the app; the cut length was 1.5 times the measured route. A reading between windows: a wiring fault at that switch; unplug the leg plug and measure ohms to ground in each position. A state that cannot be read because its device is still on the factory harness (the wiper's park contact, the gear lever's contacts): read it at its migration row in E28 and say so in a note.
record: Tick E27 in the app. No value. Note any state left to be read in E28.

goal: Every circuit in the migration table has been moved from the factory harness to the new one, one at a time and each proven alone, ending with the start circuit, and the engine has started on the new harness.
where: the whole car, one device at a time; the laptop stays on DP-DIAG in the glovebox
time: two to three full days in one stretch - confirm
tools:
Camden's Windows laptop with ECUMaster's PMU client (D-376)
USB-to-CAN interface cable (P138)
multimeter: DC volts, ohms, continuity beeper (P045)
one long meter lead, the length of the car, so one probe stays at the dash node
label printer (P041) for the MIGRATED labels
ratchet crimper for heat-shrink butt splices and rings (P171)
heat gun (P042)
contact removal tool, size 16 (P031)
insulating tape to fold back each factory end
a helper for the lamps behind you and for the first crank
before:
E27 done: all four legs plugged in, every device end waiting beside its device
E2 done: the factory odometer read and entered - it gates this row
F3 done before MG22: the display proven on the bench
Enable-at limits and inrush settings entered (E26)
Master disconnect OPEN each time a splice or terminal is made; closed to test
Wheels chocked, car on its wheels or on stands. Hands clear of the pop-ups and the wiper arms when their outputs are enabled
Fuel pump and tank work (MG20): no sparks, extinguisher within reach
First start (MG23): garage door open, belt and fan clear
know:
The order is the migration table's, by its sequence number. It is the test order: each circuit is proven alone before the next moves, so a fault shows on the circuit that caused it [work E28; D-414]
The loop for every circuit: (1) unplug the load at its factory connector, label the factory end MIGRATED and the date, tape it back; (2) connect the load to the new harness; (3) enable that one output at its enable-at value; (4) operate it and read the live current in the client; (5) measure voltage at the device under load; (6) record it [work E28]
Voltage test: load running, busbar to the device's + terminal under 0.5 V; the device's - terminal to the ground bus under 0.3 V [work E28]
Device ends: where a device has a stud or blade the new wire ends in a ring or spade; where it keeps a factory plug, the new wire joins that plug's leads with sealed heat-shrink butt splices. The two-letter factory colour says which lead takes which wire [rules device-end]
The factory harness meets itself at a few big connectors: engine harness at X-01, dash harness at X-02 and X-12, rear harness at X-03 on the left side behind the door, transmission harness at X-10. Its fuse block X-04 is under the dash. These stay together until E30 [00-CAR PT027, PT318, PT321, PT323, PT325]
Output status numbers in the client: 0 OFF, 1 ACTIVE, 2 UNDERCURRENT (a dead bulb), 3 OVERCURRENT (a tripped soft fuse), 7 THERMAL SHUTDOWN [recovery RC04]
Factory wire colours are base then tracer: GY is green with a yellow stripe; Lg is light green [00-CAR PT027]
The headlamp units in the car are LED housings fitted by a previous owner, so their current will be well under the halogen figures [00-CAR PT035]
A stalled pop-up motor pulls 15 to 25 A and the lamps move fast [work E4]
The car does not start until the last row, MG23, and is not driven until E35 [D-414; D-387]
Soft-fuse limits are set from current measured live, never from a typed guess. The measured baselines are taken at shakedown [D-025; checks CK01]
CK16 is taken after the pop-ups move and CK14 at the first crank [checks CK16, CK14]
done_when: Every migration row from MG01 to MG27 is done and each works on its own; every factory end is labelled MIGRATED with its date; the engine cranks only in P and N, starts and idles on the new harness; OIL_MIN is entered from the first idle; CK14 and CK16 are logged; a new revision is saved.
if_not: A circuit does not come up: stop there - the fault is in what you just moved. Read that output's status in the client: 3 means a shorted wire - find it, do not raise the limit; 2 means an open load or a dead bulb; no current and status 0 means the input state is wrong - watch the ladder while you work the switch. Low voltage at the device: the feed's crimp or splice. Voltage on the ground side: the ring or the star stud. The factory end is only taped back, so the circuit can go back on the factory harness while you look. If a device has no plug, stud or blade of its own to connect to without cutting the factory harness: the device-end rule says cut the plug off with 150 mm of lead, and E30 says the old harness leaves uncut - the record does not say which wins, so raise it in the app as a note before the first cut. For a PMU soft fault use recovery RC02 to RC05.
record: Tick E28 in the app when MG23 has moved and the engine has run. E2 takes the odometer reading before MG22. The per-circuit current and voltage readings, CK14's lowest cranking voltage and block offset, and CK16's readings have no row of their own: put them in a note in the app.

goal: Every circuit has been worked in one pass - key out, ACC, RUN and engine running - on the new harness alone, the limp-home procedure has been proven once, the configuration is saved as a new revision, and the whole car draws 50 mA or less asleep.
where: the whole car, in the garage with the door open; the dash node for the limp-home test; the cargo bin for the sleep reading
time: half a day, plus an hour's wait for the sleep reading - confirm
tools:
Camden's Windows laptop with ECUMaster's PMU client (D-376)
USB-to-CAN interface cable (P138)
multimeter: DC volts, ohms, continuity beeper (P045)
clamp meter that reads DC milliamps, or the multimeter in series at the disconnect
the limp-home kit: three fused jumpers 10 A, 20 A and a 5 A one with a pushbutton, a work light, the printed recovery table (P139)
a stopwatch, to time the limp-home procedure
a helper to watch the lamps at the rear
before:
E28 done: every migration row moved, the engine has started and idled
Wheels chocked; the car is not driven (the interior is out until E35)
Garage door open whenever the engine runs; belt and fan clear
For the limp-home test: engine stopped first, then master disconnect OPEN before the PMU's connector is touched
know:
The check is one pass through four key states: key out, ACC, RUN, engine running [work E29]
With the key out these still work, each by waking the PMU first: hazards, horn, each wink, brake lamps, and the interior and courtesy lamps on their own fuses [rules flasher; pins 7; fuses F12, F19]
The car goes back to sleep 30 s after the last change with the key out, both doors shut and nothing pressed. Hazards hold it awake with no limit [logic KEEP_ALIVE]
Wipers: when switched off they run on to the park position; INT is one sweep and a 3 s pause; a flick of LOW under 400 ms is one sweep; the washer pump runs only while WASH is held, then two more sweeps [rules wiper-park, washer]
Flasher rate 1.5 Hz. The hazard switch overrides the stalk [rules flasher]
Dash illumination is on with PARK and HEAD and dims; the interior lamp is on its own door switch with the key out [D-462]
The starter runs only with the lever in P or N [rules crank]
Limp-home, dead module: the PMU's 39-way is unplugged and three fused jumpers run from the busbar - 10 A onto relay K13 terminal 30 for the fuel pump, 20 A onto the O12 splice for ignition, and a 5 A pushbutton jumper onto K9's terminal 86 lead to crank, lever in P [recovery RC07]
On the jumpers the key still stops the engine by dropping K13, but there is no oil gate and no inhibitor: ignition is live whenever the disconnect is closed [recovery RC08]
If the limp-home takes more than about twenty minutes in a warm garage it will not happen at the roadside in the rain [checks CK11]
Sleeping current: 50 mA or under is accepted, 30 mA is the target. On the 40 Ah pack 150 mA is about 11 days of parking and 20 mA about 80 [checks CK02; loads LD17; D-280]
The pack gives no slow-crank warning: it is fine, then it is dead at 8.0 V [checks CK02]
done_when: Every function in the steps works first time in its key state and nothing works in a state where it should not; the engine starts and runs on the limp-home jumpers and everything is restored after; the new revision is saved in the PMU, on the laptop and on the copy for the car; one hour after key-off the car draws 50 mA or less.
if_not: A function fails: it is that circuit's migration row again - status in the client, then the ladder state, then the voltage at the device. Limp-home does not start the engine: the procedure is wrong, and now is when to find out - note exactly which jumper and which terminal failed. Sleep reading over 50 mA: with the meter still in place pull, one at a time, F1 (head unit memory), F19 (courtesy lamps), F22 (climate unit), F23 (wake stages), F12 (interior lamp), and watch for the drop; the pack's own BMS is the remainder. Do not go on to E30 on a failing sleep number.
record: Tick E29 in the app. No value on this row. The sleep reading in mA and the limp-home time in minutes have no row of their own: put both in a note.

goal: The whole factory harness is out of the car in one piece - with its fuse box, relays, control unit and the factory cluster - boxed and kept as the fallback, and the car still works on the new harness alone.
where: the whole car: under the dash, the engine bay, the left sill and the rear
tools:
sockets, spanners and screwdrivers for the harness clips and the fuse box - sizes are not in the record
trim clip tool
label printer (P041) or tags, for each connector as it comes out
camera
a box big enough to coil the harness without kinking it
multimeter: DC volts, ohms, continuity beeper (P045)
before:
E29 passed: the full function check, the limp-home test and the sleep reading
Every migration row done and every factory end labelled MIGRATED with its date
The interior is still out (D-387, D-411)
Master disconnect OPEN before the factory main feed is taken off the busbar
know:
The harness comes out INTACT. It is not cut anywhere. It is the fallback if something fails in shakedown, and refitting it is a big job [work E30; D-411]
It leaves with the factory fuse box, the relays, the control unit and the factory cluster [work E30; D-268]
The factory harness is several harnesses joined by big connectors: the front harness with the fuse block; the engine harness at X-01, a 22-cavity plug; the dash harness at X-02 and X-12; the rear harness at X-03, on the left side behind the door - check; the transmission harness at X-10, a 6-pin, and X-17, two 1-pins; the parking-brake harness at X-11 [00-CAR PT309, PT321, PT325, PT318, PT323]
The factory cluster is on two 13-cavity round connectors [00-CAR PT614]
The control unit is the box that did the flasher, the intermittent wipers and the warning chimes. The PMU does all of that now [00-CAR PT301]
The factory body grounds are X-13, at the left suspension tower and under the dash on the left, and X-14 and X-15, whose places are not in the record: follow the black wires [00-CAR PT027]
The factory main feed, with its black 1.25 sq and brown 0.3 sq fusible links, has sat on the dash-node busbar since E24, and the factory main ground on the front star since E11 [work E24, E11; 00-CAR PT316, PT317]
What stays: every device and switch the new harness uses - lamps, motors, senders, the column switches, the horn pad, the parking-brake switch, the kick-down switch and solenoid, the two release solenoids - and the wideband gauge at the node [devices; D-244]
The A/C stays as it is: compressor on the car, clutch unplugged, belt off, the rest untouched [D-474]
There is no week of driving on the old harness: the car is not driven until the interior is back [work E30]
done_when: No factory wire, fuse box, relay or control unit is left in the car; the harness is in its box in one piece with every connector labelled; nothing the new harness uses was disturbed; the car starts and every function still works.
if_not: Something is still plugged into the factory harness that no migration row moved: stop. Label it, photograph it, and raise it in the app as a note before unplugging it - it is a circuit the design does not know about. A connector that will not part: do not cut the wire; note it. A function that stopped working after the harness came out was sharing a factory ground or feed: find it now, while the harness is still in the garage.
record: Tick E30 in the app. No value. A note listing anything found still connected, and where the box is kept.

goal: The factory odometer's reading is entered in the app, in miles, before the factory cluster goes dark.
where: at the factory cluster - loose in the car with the dash out, still plugged in since E12
tools:
phone camera
a torch
before:
F3 done: the new display proven on the bench - this row's gate
Take it before E28 starts: E28 is gated on this row
know:
The factory cluster stays alive on the factory harness until the meters cutover, MG22, then goes dark and leaves the car with that harness [D-268]
The new instrument unit keeps its own odometer and starts it from this figure [work E2; D-269]
The new odometer is stored in the unit's own memory every 0.1 mile, with the memory card as a second copy, so a missing card cannot lose the mileage [D-269]
The speedometer is cable-driven, with a trip reset knob [00-CAR PT621]

Behind the dash, capped and waiting: the future-module receptacle L3-MOD and the radar receptacle L3-RDR. In the glovebox: the laptop port DP-DIAG [housings L3-MOD, L3-RDR, DP-DIAG]
Behind the driver kick panel: the sill node, with D1 and D2, relays K5 to K8 and the fuse holders F8, F9 (empty) and F14. Behind both kick panels: a capped speaker receptacle [devices DV43; housings L3-SPF-L, L3-SPF-R]
Under the carpet: the seat harnesses to four capped receptacles under the seats, the audio cables along both sills, the sill run, and in the tunnel the 2 AWG feed, two 1/0 cables, the rear leg and a pull string [routes RT27, RT28, RT30, RT32, RT19, RT15]
Water: every conductor enters a node from below or with a drip loop; nothing in the lowest 50 mm of the footwell. Whatever the look at the cowl drains found at the measurement day applies now [rules water-ingress; checks CK04]
The factory dash parts, from the manual's exploded view: steering wheel and nut, upper and lower column covers, grilles, switch panels, ventilator louvers, glove compartment and lid, centre panel, radio cover, meter hood, the instrument panel itself on 4 bolts with sets of 2 and 3 bolts beside it, coin box, rear console, shift lever knob [S-002 p.14-2]
That view is the 1985 car - confirm on the car; the strip's own photos and bags are the better guide [S-002 p.14-2]
Seat-belt anchor bolts: 39 to 55 N-m. Steering wheel nut: 40 to 50 N-m. Seat mounting bolts: the manual says check them for looseness and gives no figure [S-002 p.14-4; 00-CAR SP-174; S-002 p.14-3]
done_when: Every panel, the seats and the cargo trim are back with no fastener left in a bag; the finished harness runs are photographed; with the car whole every function of E29 works; the laptop port, the fuse blocks, the PMU's lever and the master disconnect can still be reached.
if_not: A function that worked at E29 fails now: a wire was pinched or a plug knocked by the last panel fitted - take that panel back off. A panel will not seat over a loom: move the loom, never force the panel. A plug or fuse that can no longer be reached with the trim on: stop and re-route now, it only gets harder. A leftover fastener: find its hole; the strip's bags are labelled by panel.
record: Tick E35 in the app. No value. The car may now be driven: the first drive is E31.

goal: The car has been driven cold, at night, in the wet and on one long run with the log recording, and the log shows no fault, no tripped output and no channel near its limit.
where: on the road; the garage before and after each drive
time: four drives over a week or more - they wait on the weather
tools:
phone with the Rx7 app, to pull each drive's log from the instrument unit
phone with the battery's own app, to watch the pack
Camden's Windows laptop with ECUMaster's PMU client (D-376)
USB-to-CAN interface cable (P138)
multimeter: DC volts, ohms, continuity beeper (P045)
the limp-home kit and the printed recovery table in the car from the first drive (P139)
warning beacons
before:
E35 done: the interior is back
E30 done: the factory harness is out. It stays boxed until this shakedown is passed
The laptop, cable and limp-home kit ride in the car on every one of these drives
Know recovery RC01 by heart before the first drive: the master disconnect is the only certain off
know:
Four conditions: a cold start on a cold morning; a night drive; a wet drive; a long drive. Logging on for all of them [work E31]
The instrument unit writes every drive to its card: a thinned record once a second of every channel, and the full bus log. The app pulls the thinned log over Bluetooth, an hour's drive in under a minute [log_channels; params log_pull_s_per_hour; D-493]
Battery voltage: charging should sit between 13.8 and 14.6 V. The pack's ceiling is 14.6 V; the factory regulator's own band reaches 15.2 V, so watch the top. The PMU warns below 12.0 V and above 15.0 V [work E42; checks CK03; 00-CAR SP-081; rules voltage]
Cranking sags to about 10.5 V. Loads are shed only after about 10 s under 11.5 V and never during START, so the display must not reboot on a crank [rules voltage; D-463]
The pack heats itself in the cold only from a charging source; how much it draws is not published. That is what to watch in the battery app on the cold morning [00-CAR SP-233]
Per-channel current is logged for all 22 outputs. Each channel's peak is compared with its limit [log_channels LC15; work E31]
Limits in the record's own figures: water temperature 105 C, oil pressure 1.0 bar low mark, redline 7000 rpm [params hot_water_c, low_oil_bar, redline_rpm]
Fault channels that must stay zero: global fault, trip state, input faults; and CAN health must stay good [log_channels LC05, LC14, LC09, LC26]
Stuck-on check: commanded off, each of O2, O3, O5, O7 and O12 must read zero volts. Battery volts on an output that is off is a shorted switch, and only the master disconnect kills it [checks CK07]
Ground offset between the engine block and the dash ground bus should be under 50 mV, idling and at full electrical load [checks CK05]
An engine that starts and dies about 3 s later with zero oil pressure shown is the oil gate doing its job, not a PMU fault [recovery RC02]
With a dead module the car has no lights, wipers or horn: a limp home is daylight, dry and short. If stopped and dark, beacons out first [recovery RC09]
done_when: All four drives are done; each one's log is in the app; no drive shows a fault flag, a tripped or retrying output, an input fault or a lost bus; charging stayed at or under 14.6 V; every channel's peak is under its limit; the stuck-on and ground-offset checks pass.
if_not: A fault on the road: recovery RC01 first - stop, engine off, disconnect open - then RC02 to tell a soft fault from a dead module. A tripped channel: do not raise its limit on the roadside beyond what gets you home, and write down what you changed (RC05). Charging above 14.6 V: stop the shakedown - the fix is the alternator's regulator, never the battery. Ground offset over 50 mV: note it; it decides a sensor return wire at the engine swap. Anything that fails in a way the new harness cannot be made to cure: the boxed factory harness is the fallback, and that is a decision to raise in the app, not to take alone.
record: Tick E31 in the app when all four drives are logged. No value. The drives themselves are logged from the app; the stuck-on and ground-offset readings go in a note.

goal: Every output's steady current has been measured live and written down, every limit that was still at its channel cap is set from a measurement, and the configuration is saved as a new revision.
where: in the garage: laptop on DP-DIAG, engine running for the lamp and charging readings
tools:
Camden's Windows laptop with ECUMaster's PMU client (D-376)
USB-to-CAN interface cable (P138)
multimeter: DC volts, ohms, continuity beeper (P045)
pen and paper or the phone, for one figure per output
a helper to work switches
before:
E31 done: the four shakedown drives logged
Garage door open; wheels chocked; belt and fan clear
Stand clear of the pop-ups and the wiper arms while they are cycled
know:
Limits are set from current measured live in the client, never from a typed guess [D-025]
The class factors: motors, stall current x 1.1; lamps, running current x 1.35; resistive loads, cold current x 1.2; electronics, running current x 1.5 [work E32]
How to take each baseline: lamps warm, after two seconds, not the switch-on surge; motors mid-travel, not stalled [checks CK01]
A reading more than about 20 percent under the expected figure is a tired part, not a bad reading: that gap is the replacement list. A reading over the expected figure is a fault to find before the limit is set [checks CK01]
Expected running amps: O1 9.5 - O2 7.4 - O3 8.9 - O4 11.5 - O5 2.0 - O6 4.4 - O7 3.9 - O8 4.0 - O9 5.5 - O10 10.0 - O11 6.0 - O12 10 - O17 4.2 - O18 4.2 - O19 3.9 - O20 1.5 - O21 0.2 - O22 0.2 [pins est_a]
The headlamps are LED units a previous owner fitted, so O2 and O3 will read far under the halogen figures. That is the lamp, not a fault [00-CAR PT035]
Limits still at the channel's cap: O1 25.0, O4 25.0, O8 13.0, O9 13.0, O10 13.0, O11 13.0, O12 25.0, O19 7.0, O20 7.0, O21 7.0, O22 7.0. O2 and O3 sit at 13.0, the 14 AWG branch's ceiling. Already set from a measurement: O5 4.0, O6 7.5, O7 11, O17 4.5, O18 4.5 [pins enable_a, enable_basis]
No limit may go above what the pin and wire carry: 25 A pins, 15 A pins, 7 A pins; 13 A on the headlamp branches [pins hw_max_a; D-243]
Pop-up stall was measured at 12.8 and 13.1 A per side. Both on O1 is 25.9 A, and x 1.1 is 28.5 A - above the pin - so O1 stays at 25.0 [loads LD08; pins 38]
Wiper stall is a design range, 12 to 20 A, never measured [loads LD07]
O21 and O22 sit under the PMU's own measuring floor: expect zero, record zero, give them no band [checks CK01]
Health band: a lamp channel warns below half its baseline, a motor channel above one and a half times it. The low half is the PMU's Min Current setting, which only warns and never switches off. A channel whose baseline is under four times the pin's measuring floor gets no band [rules health-band]
done_when: One steady figure is written down for every live output; every limit that can be set from a measurement has been; each output has been worked again from cold and none trips; the new revision is saved in the PMU, on the laptop and on the car's copy.
if_not: A baseline over the expected figure: find the fault before setting any limit from it. A channel trips after its limit is tightened: the factor was applied to a warm reading or the inrush window is too short - go back to the previous limit, read again, and note it. A channel whose class is not obvious (the horn, ignition, the relay coils, the comfort bus): the record does not say - leave it at its cap and note it rather than guess.
record: Tick E32 in the app. No value on this row. Send the measured current for each output in a note, one line per output: it becomes the baseline and the measured figure in the record.

goal: After the first heat cycles every heavy lug and stud has been re-torqued and paint-marked, the cranking voltage drops are still under 0.5 V, the engine-bay looms are final-wrapped and tied down, and every grommet is sealed.
where: cargo bin, dash node, engine bay, front star on the radiator support, driver sill
tools:
torque wrench 1/4 in drive, 2-20 N-m (P046), and a larger one for the battery posts and the starter stud
the torque figures written at D1 from each maker's sheet
paint pen and cavity wax (P082)
multimeter: DC volts, ohms, continuity beeper (P045)
cloth harness tape (P080), loom and P-clips (P081), clear heat-shrink (P076)
heat gun (P042)
a helper on the key for the cranking readings
before:
E32 done; the car has been through several full warm-ups and cool-downs
Engine cold
Master disconnect OPEN for every stud. Close it only for the cranking readings
Rings and watch off; boots back on every lug before the disconnect is closed
know:
Every heavy connection is torqued to its maker's figure, read off the maker's sheet. The record holds no figure yet - confirm each from the sheet [rules torque]
Cargo bin: both battery post clamps; the master disconnect's input stud (the 1/0 from the battery) and output stud (the 2 AWG lug, the starter's fuse holder, and the amplifier's holder if fitted); both studs of the Class-T block; the rear ground stud, where the battery negative, the cranking return and the rear returns land [backbone B1, B2, B5, B7, B8; cables C01, C05, C11, C12]
Dash node: the busbar stud with the main feed and the link to the PMU; the PMU's +12 V stud and its 39-way connector's screws; the ground bus to the dash star; the fuse holders at the bar [cables C03, C10; grounds G14; rules torque]
Engine bay: the starter's main stud with the 1/0 cable and the two bolt-down fuse holders F17 and F18; the starter's small S terminal; the alternator's output stud; on the block, the 1/0 cranking return and the 2 AWG strap, both ends; relay K9's socket [backbone B2, B3, B4, B6, B7; cables C04, C06, C07, C08, C09]
Star studs: front on the radiator support, dash, rear in the cargo bin, and the sill [grounds G05, G14, G23, G33]
Voltage drop while cranking: battery + post to the starter's main stud, and battery - post to the engine block, each under 0.5 V. Near 0.5 V means a bad crimp. The first readings are on rows E43 and E44 [work E12, E43, E44]
The cabin looms were final-wrapped at E35. Only the engine bay's are wrapped now [work E33]
The shielded tach wire crosses ignition leads at 90 degrees and never runs beside one within 50 mm: hold that when wrapping [rules emc-routing]
Engine-bay labels get clear heat-shrink over them before the wrap [rules label-format]
The legs pass the firewall on the passenger side (engine leg) and the cowl (front leg); the heavy cables and the rear leg run in the tunnel [routes RT01, RT06, RT15]
A ground stud is bare metal, star washer, torque, then cavity wax over the joint [backbone B5]
done_when: Every stud on the list is at its maker's torque with a fresh paint mark; both cranking drops are under 0.5 V and no worse than at E12; the engine-bay looms are wrapped, clipped and clear of heat and moving parts; every grommet is seated and sealed; the car starts and charges as before.
if_not: A nut that turns a long way before it reaches torque was loose: look at the lug and the stud for heat marks, and note which one. A drop near or over 0.5 V: find it by measuring across each joint in that path while cranking - the joint with the voltage across it is the bad one. A lug that has gone blue or a boot that has melted: stop, do not drive, note it. A torque figure you cannot find on any maker's sheet: note it - do not guess.
record: Tick E33 in the app. No value on this row. The two new cranking drops, in volts, go in a note beside E43 and E44's first readings.

goal: The final configuration is backed up, and the car carries everything needed to fix it at the roadside: the limp-home kit, the printed tables, spare contacts, the removal tools and spare fuses.
where: desk for the backup and the printing; the glovebox for the kit
tools:
Camden's Windows laptop with ECUMaster's PMU client (D-376)
USB-to-CAN interface cable (P138)
a printer, and a laminator or plastic sleeves
a bag or box that fits the glovebox
before:
E33 done
The configuration in the PMU is the one saved at E32
know:
The limp-home kit: three fused jumpers with the node's own terminals on their ends - 10 A for the pump, 20 A for ignition, 5 A with a pushbutton for cranking - the USB-to-CAN cable with the current configuration file, a work light and the printed recovery table. It lives in the glovebox beside the laptop port [parts P139]
None of the kit is ever fitted to the car. A limp-home wire left in place is the next fault [recovery RC10]
The bag also holds the beacons: with a dead module the car has no lights, and being stopped and dark is the real hazard [recovery RC09, RC10]
The recovery procedure is ten rows, RC01 to RC10. Printed from the record, the copy in the glovebox cannot drift from the design [recovery; D-344]
The pin table and the cavity table go in the car as printouts, with the fuse and output map: one copy at the dash node and one in the glovebox, laminated [work E34; rules fuse-lid-card]
A plastic size-16 contact removal tool lives in the car. The DTP power plugs need the size-12 tool [parts P032, P033]
Spare contacts: size-16 sockets and pins, the 14 AWG versions, and size-12 sockets and pins [parts P022, P023, P024, P025, P026, P027]
Five blade fuses of each value in the car. The values fitted are 2, 3, 5, 7.5 and 10 A, with 20 A for the window feeds when they are fused [work E34; fuses F2, F3, F15, F1, F8]
The bigger fuses have one spare each on their parts rows: 25 A and 40 A MAXI, 30 A and 100 A MIDI, the 150 A Class-T [parts P191, P190, P054, P055, P048]
Saved configuration files come back to the project by hand [D-376]
After this row the project is ready for your ruling that electrical is done (E48), and then for the fold into the car's own record (E49) [work E34, E48]
done_when: The final configuration file exists in the PMU, on the laptop, in the glovebox kit and in the project; the kit bag is in the glovebox with every item on the list; the printed tables are in the car; the spare contacts, tools and fuses are in the car.
if_not: The kit does not fit the glovebox with the laptop port usable: the port wins - move the spares and printouts elsewhere in the car and note where. A printout that does not match what is in the car: the car is right and the record is wrong - raise it in the app as a note, it must be fixed before E48.
record: Tick E34 in the app. No value. A note if anything in the kit is missing or kept somewhere other than the glovebox.

goal: You have ruled the electrical project done: the new harness is in, the shakedown is passed, nothing is open, and the car as it now stands is the baseline.
where: desk, with the app open; one last look at the car
tools:
the Rx7 app
the notes you wrote at E28, E29, E31, E32 and E33
before:
E34 done - this row's gate, and through it every row before it
Every reading you put in a note has been applied to the record by a run
know:
This is your ruling, like the design freeze. Nobody else ticks it [work E48; D-533]
After it a run folds the project into the car: the as-built harness, fuses, channels, connectors and service instructions become the car's own record, and the project is archived [work E49]
The list cannot have gone vague on the way here: every row before this one had to be done for this one to open [D-533]
What 'passed' means for each check: sleeping current 50 mA or under; charging 14.6 V or under; block-to-dash ground offset under 50 mV; stuck-on outputs read zero; the limp-home procedure proven once; the crank log clean with block offset under 0.74 V; the pop-up cycle clean; a measured baseline for every output [checks CK02, CK03, CK05, CK07, CK11, CK14, CK16, CK01]
Cranking drops under 0.5 V on both sides, first and after the heat cycles [work E43, E44, E33]
The boxed factory harness was kept as the fallback until shakedown was passed. What happens to it afterwards is not in the record - confirm [D-411]
Still capped and waiting for other projects, and not part of this ruling: the window fuses, the seats, the heater servos and blower, the radar, the amplifier and speakers, the swap's reserved outputs [fuses F8, F34; pins 1, 14; housings L3-SD]
Open questions only you can answer live in the app's blocks. None may be open in electrical when you tick [D-533]
done_when: Every item in the steps is true, and E48 is ticked in the app.
if_not: Any item is not true: do not tick. Fix it, or raise it in the app as a note so it becomes a row - the fold copies whatever the record says into the car's baseline, wrong or right. A difference between the car and the record that you know about but never wrote down: write it now.
record: Tick E48 in the app. That is the ruling. Nothing else is entered; the fold (E49) is then started from the app.

goal: Every factory wire the new harness lands on has been seen on the car, and its colour either matches the 1982 diagram or the difference is written down.
where: engine bay, under the car at the transmission, the tank sender at the rear, the handbrake lever
tools:
multimeter on ohms / continuity
torch and a small mirror
phone camera
masking tape and a marker
jack, jack stands and wheel chocks (for the inhibitor switch and the tank sender)
before:
S1 (the strip) is done and C1 (the measurement day) is under way: the handbrake lever and the rear floor are bare
V-114 is answered: CK08 (pop-up motors) and CK09 (wiper motor) are the other half of this row
Battery negative disconnected: the alternator's B stud beside the A-08 plug is always live
Engine cold: the two senders are on the engine's rear housing
Car on jack stands with the wheels chocked before you go under it
know:
The desk half is done: every wire colour the design names was read off the 1982 diagram scans, and all were right. Nobody has compared the diagram with this car yet. [D-348]
Factory colour codes: the first letter is the base colour, the second the tracer stripe. B black, W white, R red, G green, Y yellow, L blue, Br brown, O orange, Lg light green. GY is green with a yellow tracer, not grey. [01-INTAKE factory-circuits README, wire colour codes]
Alternator plug A-08 has two wires: BW is the regulator's ignition feed (the new wire is L1-S1 2), WB is the charge-lamp line (the new wire is L1-S2 8). [00-CAR PT025-R, PT025-L; cavities L1-S1 2, L1-S2 8]
Inhibitor switch A-06 (the park / neutral and reverse switch on the automatic) has four wires: BY in and BW out are the starter interlock, GY in and RW out feed the reverse lamps. [00-CAR PT298-BY, PT298-BW, PT298-GY, PT298-RW; devices DV05]
Water temperature sender C-02: one spade, wire YW, in the rear housing directly below the oil pressure sender. [devices DV06; 00-CAR PT023-YW]
Oil pressure sender C-09: one spade, wire BrY, in the rear-housing gauge port, above the water temperature sender. [devices DV07; 00-CAR PT004-signal]
Brake fluid level switch C-05 on the reservoir: two wires, BR and B. [00-CAR PT562-BR, PT562-B; cavities L1-S2 1]
Parking brake switch C-04: one wire, BR; the switch body grounds through the lever bracket. [cavities L3-S2 11]
Fuel tank sender C-01: Y is the signal, B the ground. [00-CAR PT169-Y, PT169-B; cavities L4-S 1]
A 44-year-old harness has been repaired. Where the car and the diagram disagree, the car is right and the row is changed. [D-348; CLAUDE.md R11]
done_when: Each of the seven connectors (A-08, A-06, C-02, C-09, C-05, C-04, C-01) has a photo and one line: the colours seen, and 'matches' or what differs.
if_not: A colour that differs, a missing wire or a previous owner's splice: do not trace it and do not cut it. Photograph it, write what you see in the app and carry on. The agent changes the row before any leg is crimped.
record: Tick A5. In the answer's words give one line per connector with the colours you saw. The CK08 and CK09 readings belong to V-114.

goal: The alternator's rated output, read off its own case, is in the record.
where: engine bay, at the alternator
tools:
torch
rag and a soft brush
small mirror or the phone camera
before:
Engine off and cold, key out
Battery negative disconnected before a hand or a tool goes near the back of the alternator: its B stud is always live
know:
The case has been looked at once and read only 'B' and Mitsubishi. The rating was not found. [work V-002]
The 1982 factory data gives 12 V 50 A for this car. [00-CAR SP-079, S-038 T:3]
The 1985 manual gives 55 A, Mitsubishi A5T30574 - a later car's unit. [00-CAR SP-078, S-002 p.5-3]
The 1981-83 parts catalogue number is N221-18-300R; the catalogue prints no amp rating. [00-CAR SP-006]
Replacement units carry Mitsubishi A2T, A3T or A5T numbers; that number identifies the unit even where no rating is stamped. [00-CAR PT025]
At the back: B is the output stud (wire WR, always live), a two-pin coupler holds R (BW) and L (WB), and a test hole about 20 mm deep sits near B. [00-CAR PT025-B, PT025-R, PT025-L, PT025-F]
Nothing in the new harness depends on the figure: the alternator fuse F18 is 100 A on a 6 AWG cable. [fuses F18; cables C07]
It is the yardstick for the charging reading after the first start on the new backbone, and for the no-charge fault seen earlier (11.4 V at idle). [checks CK03; D-198]
done_when: A rating in amps read off the case is entered, or the Mitsubishi number on the case with a photo.
if_not: No rating anywhere: enter the Mitsubishi number (A2T, A3T or A5T and its digits) in words with a photo, and the agent finds the rating from it. No number either: say so. The record then keeps 50 A (SP-079) as the book figure, not a reading.
record: V-002 takes a value in A. A part number, if that is all there is, goes in the answer's words.

goal: One email to Ionic has asked the four open questions about the battery, and their reply is in the app.
where: desk
time: 20 min to write; the reply is theirs
tools: email
before: Nothing. This can be sent today
know:
The pack is an Ionic IC-12V40-S9H: 12 V, 40 Ah, heated LiFePO4, four cells in series. [D-330]
What already works: the BMS answers on Bluetooth service FFE0, characteristic FFE1. A read returns a frame - 7E start, 01 type, 08 length, four little-endian 16-bit cell counts, a checksum, 0D - which decodes at about 1.43 mV per count. [D-330]
Current and state of charge are not in that frame. Until Ionic answers, the car logs voltage only; no shunt was bought. [D-330]
Published figures: charge to 14.6 V +/- 0.1, float 13.9 V, discharge cut-off 8.0 V, operating -20 to 60 C. [00-CAR SP-231, SP-232, SP-233]
The heater's own figures are not published. Packs of this class heat only from an active charger, but that is unverified for the S9H. [00-CAR SP-233; work V-052]
If the BMS disconnects the pack while the engine runs, the alternator loses its load in an instant; a surge clamp (P136) is in the design for that case. [work W-330b; parts P136]
The engine project plans a 160 A alternator, which can push well over 100 A into the pack after a long crank. [work W-330b]
Ionic's support address is not in the record. [00-CAR suppliers - no Ionic row]
done_when: The email is sent and Ionic's reply, word for word, is pasted into the app.
if_not: No reply: note the date you sent it and send once more. If Ionic will not answer, say so in the app as a note. The row stays open and the agent decides what the design assumes; the figures stay unverified.
record: Tick W-330b when the reply is in, with the reply pasted whole into the answer's words. The agent's row V-052 reads it.

goal: The PMU's own current draw when it is switched off, measured on the bench, is in the record in mA.
where: bench
tools:
12 V bench supply (any steady 12 V source; not a parts row)
multimeter with a mA range, wired in series (P045 is the cart's meter; any meter in hand will do)
a fused lead with a small fuse (the record gives no size for this test)
two short leads fitted with the PMU's own terminals, for pins 25 and 7
a ring lug or a clamp for the PMU's M6 stud
before:
The PMU-24 DL is on the bench with nothing wired to its outputs
Do this in the same sitting as F-009: the set-up is the same
Rings and watch off; the supply off while you connect
know:
The design budget assumes the sleeping PMU draws 150 mA. One bench report of an ECUMaster PMU says under 20 mA, and ECUMaster publishes no figure. [loads LD17; D-280]
On the 40 Ah pack that is about 11 days of parking at 150 mA against about 80 days at 20 mA, before the battery's own protection cuts off at 8.0 V with no slow-crank warning first. [D-280; 00-CAR SP-232]
The whole car asleep must be 30 mA or under, 50 mA at most; that is measured later in the car. This reading is the PMU's share of it. [checks CK02; D-280]
Power goes in on the M6 stud in the middle of the unit. Ground is pin 25. Pin 7 (+12 V SW) switches the PMU on and off. [pins STUD, 25, 7; S-027; S-028 p.8]

know:
The PMU sends CAN frames two ways. Its Standard CAN Stream is fixed by ECUMaster. Its CANbus Export is ours to define, and 0x100-0x130 are Exports. [D-378; S-028 p.90, p.95]
An Export field can be 8-bit unsigned, 8-bit signed, 16-bit big endian or 16-bit little endian, times a whole multiplier from 1 to 1000, or the raw value. A frame is 0 to 8 bytes, sent 1 to 100 times a second or on an edge. [S-028 p.90-92]
The manual shows no bit-packing, no multiplexing and no rolling counter on an Export. Those three are what this row proves or rules out. [D-378]
Our four frames go out on CAN2 at 500 kbps, little-endian: 0x100 vehicle state at 20 Hz, 0x110 power at 10 Hz, 0x120 outputs at 5 Hz, 0x130 per-channel current at 5 Hz. [can_messages 0x100, 0x110, 0x120, 0x130; params can_bitrate; can_map.h]
The laptop talks to the PMU on CAN1: PMU pin 23 is CAN1 high, pin 36 CAN1 low; on the interface's DB9 plug pin 7 is CAN high and pin 2 CAN low. CAN1 has no terminator inside the PMU, so a 120 ohm resistor goes across the pair. [pins 23, 36; S-028 p.36-38]
Never connect the interface's +5 V to the PMU's +5 V pin. [S-028 p.37]
Status LED: steady orange means the PMU is active and connected to the PC. [S-028 p.14]
Whatever cannot be built becomes a simpler layout - one byte per field, fixed frames in place of 0x130's index. The agent changes the record first and the firmware second. [work F-009]
Two extras the control panel wants if the client can export them: input A8's decoded state (idle, horn, hazard, wink L, wink R) and output O20's dimmer duty. Bytes 5-6 of 0x110 are kept for them. [work F-009; D-492]
The client is only on the Windows laptop; files it saves come back to the project by hand. [D-376]
Seeing the bytes on the wire needs a listener on CAN2. The record does not name one for this session. [work B8 - the bench bus is not built yet]
done_when: For each of these you can say yes or no, with what the client showed: a packed bitfield byte, a rolling 0-255 counter in byte 7, a multiplexed 0x130, the two panel extras; and CK06, CK13 and CK15 each have an answer.
if_not: The client cannot do something: that is a result, not a failure. Write exactly what it offered instead. The client will not connect: check the 120 ohm resistor is across pins 23 and 36, the two CAN wires are not swapped, and the PMU's LED is lit. Do not change any other setting in the PMU to make an Export work.
